title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 119 (Inspection of minute-books of general meeting)

content.overview: The books containing the minutes of the proceedings of any general meeting of a company or of a resolution passed by postal ballot shall be kept at the registered office and shall be open, during business hours, to inspection by any member without charge, subject to reasonable restrictions as the company may impose. Any member shall be entitled to be furnished, within seven days after he has made a request, with a copy of any minutes on payment of the prescribed fee. On unlawful refusal, the NCLT may direct inspection or supply of a copy.
content.glance: General-meeting minute-books are kept at the registered office and open to member inspection; copies are available on payment of the prescribed fee within seven days.
content.study:
## Section 119 — Inspection of minute-books of general meeting

**Inspection.** Minute-books of general meetings (and postal-ballot resolutions) must be kept at the registered office and be open to inspection by members during business hours, subject to the Act and reasonable restrictions.

**Copies.** A member may request a copy on payment of the prescribed fee. The company must supply the copy within seven days under section 119(2).

**Tribunal remedy.** Where the company refuses inspection or a copy without lawful basis, the member may apply to the NCLT, which may direct immediate inspection or supply of the copy.

**Limits.** Section 119 is not a general right to inspect Board minutes. Distinguish from the evidentiary role of minutes under section 118.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.
